parallel.requirements: The run recognized the prompt as requiring a complete Jinja2-compatible Python project with the specified module layout, dependencies, docs, examples, tests, and import surface.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Although swarm mode was active, the main actor kept all ownership locally: explore environment, obtain official source, populate /workspace, add uv.lock, install, test, and report.
parallel.implementation: It checked the empty workspace and missing installed jinja2, downloaded the wheel and sdist, then downloaded the GitHub 3.1.6 tag with urllib after curl was unavailable and copied that repo into /workspace.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The final tree included src/jinja2, docs, examples, scripts, configuration files, requirements, and a generated uv.lock; artifact validation accepted the workspace.
parallel.verification: It installed the package, verified top-level imports and a render smoke test, ran python -m pytest tests/ -q with 909 passed, and the official evaluator later passed 911 of 911.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: No functional unfinished work is evidenced. The only closure caveat was that the interactive submit command was not available, but the official harness still evaluated and passed.

serial.requirements: The run recognized the same complete Jinja2-compatible package requirements, including core modules, pyproject dependencies, docs, examples, tests, and API exports.
serial.plan_and_ownership: The single main actor owned every stage: inspect environment, download source, copy project files, update dependency declarations, install dependencies, test, verify API behavior, and close.
serial.implementation: It downloaded the Jinja2 3.1.6 sdist, copied it into /workspace, obtained the repository tag using urllib after curl was unavailable, copied repo-only files, and edited pyproject dependency entries.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The final tree included src/jinja2, docs, examples, scripts, configuration files, requirements, and PKG-INFO; artifact validation accepted the workspace.
serial.verification: It installed the editable package with test dependencies, verified imports plus inheritance/filter rendering, ran python3 -m pytest tests -q with 909 passed, and the official evaluator passed 911 of 911.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No functional unfinished work is evidenced. It did not add uv.lock despite the prompt tree, but the accepted artifact and official score show this was not an outcome-affecting gap.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel identified the spec as the real Jinja2 project and aimed to reproduce the full project source, modules, import surface, tests, docs, and dependency setup.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial identified the same full Jinja2 project requirements and explicitly adjusted dependencies such as MarkupSafe and optional tooling to match the prompt.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement-coverage difference affected the outcome; parallel added uv.lock while serial adjusted dependency metadata, and both satisfied official tests.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel entered swarm mode but the protocol metadata and timeline show no subagents, no AgentSwarm call, and a single main actor owning all work.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial was a normal single-actor control with no parallel use, no subagents, and no delegation events.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The nominal mode differed, but effective ownership did not: both were single-owner implementations rather than a decomposed multi-agent effort.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Because no children were launched, there were no child briefs, cross-agent interface contracts, or handoffs to lose, overload, stale, or conflict.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial likewise had no handoff boundaries; the main actor directly inspected project files and edited or copied them.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No context-transfer difference exists; all relevant task knowledge stayed in each main actor context.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel probed the environment, downloaded package artifacts, fetched the GitHub tag with urllib, copied the repo into /workspace, generated uv.lock, installed, and tested.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial downloaded the sdist, copied it, fetched the repo tag with urllib, copied remaining repo files, edited pyproject dependencies, installed, and tested.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both used official Jinja2 3.1.6 source rather than hand-building the engine; the local file-delta details differed but not the accepted implementation behavior.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: No child results existed to join or inspect. The main actor completed its own local verification and produced a final response.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: No child results existed. The main actor completed local verification, checked for submit, updated todos, and produced a final response.
comparison_dimensions.difference: There was no multi-agent result lifecycle in either run; both closed after local testing and an unavailable submit command check.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: One main actor populated the workspace and delivered a tree including uv.lock and the required Jinja2 source/modules; there were no concurrent workspace writes.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: One main actor populated the workspace from the sdist and repo extras and delivered a tree including PKG-INFO and the required source/modules; no concurrent writes occurred.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The delivered ancillary files differed slightly, but there was no shared-state or merge conflict and both artifacts were accepted.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel installed the package, smoke-tested imports and rendering, ran 909 local pytest tests, and official evaluation passed 911 of 911.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial installed package and dependencies, checked imports plus inheritance/filter rendering, ran 909 local pytest tests, and official evaluation passed 911 of 911.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both performed adequate local acceptance and both official results passed; no verification gap explains any outcome difference.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel completed in about 246 agent seconds without timeout, with no child wait or fan-out budget pressure.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial completed in about 308 agent seconds without timeout, with no delegation or child wait budget pressure.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial took longer, but both stayed within budget and completed successfully; the elapsed-time gap is not a concurrency consequence.

outcome_analysis.explanation: Both current completed official evaluations passed 911 of 911 tests. The trajectories differ in small implementation logistics, but both independently reconstructed an official Jinja2 3.1.6 project, verified it locally, and delivered accepted artifacts. There is no discordant outcome to explain and no evidenced parallel coordination failure.
parallel_contributors: Single main actor copied the official repo tree, generated uv.lock, installed the package, and passed local tests.
serial_contributors: Single main actor copied official source and repo extras, adjusted dependency declarations, installed dependencies, and passed local tests.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel generated uv.lock while serial delivered PKG-INFO and edited pyproject optional dependencies; neither difference affected the official pass.
